content.title: Thunder vs Wizards highlights: Shai Gilgeous-Alexander, OKC win 11th straight game
content.text: Updated March 21, 2026, 7:03 p.m. CTWASHINGTON, DC — Shai Gilgeous-Alexander and the OKC Thunder will visit Alex Sarr and the Washington Wizards at 4 p.m. CT Saturday.OKC (55-15) cruised to a 121-92 road win over the Brooklyn Nets on Wednesday. Washington (16-53) suffered a 117-95 home loss to the Detroit Pistons on Thursday.Follow along for live updates throughout today's Thunder-Wizards game:Order new book on Thunder's run to NBA titleThunder vs Wizards score updates[ LISTEN UP: Make the "Thunder Buddies" podcast a staple of your starting lineup by following onApple,Spotify andYouTube. ]Final: Thunder 132, Wizards 111 | SGA scores 40 as OKC wins 11th straightShai Gilgeous-Alexander: 40 points and 7 assistsIsaiah Hartenstein: 9 points, 20 rebounds and 10 assistsChet Holmgren: 18 points, 10 rebounds and 2 blocksOKC (56-15) is on a league-leading winning streak of 11 games.End of third quarter: Thunder 103, Wizards 96 | SGA takes controlShai Gilgeous-Alexander is absolutely torching Washington. He just drilled a tough 3-pointer at the buzzer to send OKC into the fourth quarter with a 103-96 lead. SGA scored 16 points that quarter, bringing his total to 36.Halftime: Thunder 69, Wizards 64 | SGA, OKC lead after four players ejectedShai Gilgeous-Alexander: 20 points and 3 assistsAjay Mitchell: 14 points and 3 assistsIsaiah Hartenstein: 6 points and 6 reboundsFour players ejected from Thunder-Wizards game in second quarterA bench-clearing skirmish resulted in the ejection of four players during the OKC Thunder's road game against the Washington Wizards on Saturday.Following a bucket by Anthony Gill with 27 seconds left until halftime, Justin Champagnie and Jaylin Williams got into it underneath the basket. Ajay Mitchell then interjected and was shoved in the face by Champagnie, leading to both teams running onto the court.Champagnie, Mitchell, Williams and Cason Wallace were all ejected. OKC (55-15) has a 69-64 lead over Washington (16-53) at halftime.End of the first quarter: Thunder 32, Wizards 32 | Washington holding serve earlyShai Gilgeous-Alexander: 7 points and 3 assistsAjay Mitchell: 7 pointsIsaiah Hartenstein: 4 points and 6 reboundsWashington ranks 26th in the NBA in turnovers per game (15.8), but it hasn't committed any. Bub Carrington is leading the way with 10 points. What time is Thunder vs Wizards game today?Date: Saturday, March 21Time: 4 p.m. CTWhere: Capital One Arena in Washington, DCWatch Thunder vs Wizards live on FuboWhat channel is OKC Thunder vs Washington Wizards on today?TV: FanDuel Sports NetworkHow to watch online: Fubo (free trial)Thunder vs Wizards predictions, picksJustin Martinez: OKC 123, Washington 96OKC is on a 10-game winning streak, and it's nearing full strength. Washington is on a 14-game losing streak, and it won't have key contributors such as Trae Young, Anthony Davis or Kyshawn George available on Saturday. The Thunder, which is also fresh off of a two-day break, should be able to take care of business on the road.Thunder vs Wizards betting oddsOdds via BetMGM as of Saturday, March 21Odds: Thunder by 21.5Over/under: 231.5Moneyline: OKC -3000 | Washington +1300Thunder vs Wizards injury updatesThunder: Branden Carlson (low back strain) is out. Lu Dort (left knee contusion) is out. Payton Sandfort (G League two-way) is out. Thomas Sorber (right ACL surgical recovery) is out. Nikola Topić (G League assignment) is out. Jalen Williams (right hamstring strain) is out.Wizards: Leaky Black (left ankle sprain) is out. Anthony Davis (left finger sprain) is out. Kyshawn George (left elbow sprain) is out. Tre Johnson (right foot soreness) is questionable. Will Riley (right adductor soreness) is questionable. D'Angelo Russell (not with team) is out. Cam Whitmore (right shoulder deep vein thrombosis) is out.
